citation.authors: Haldar S, Egli L, De Castro CA, et al.
citation.title: High or low glycemic index (GI) meals at dinner results in greater postprandial glycemia compared with breakfast: a randomized controlled trial

population.description: 34 per-protocol completers (48 enrolled) of a crossover trial in 'healthy, Chinese, elderly volunteers', Singapore: 21 men and 13 postmenopausal women (Table 1). Enrolment: Chinese ethnic origin, 50-70 y, BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2; excluded smoking, waist >90 cm (men) / >85 cm (women), BP >=150/90 mm Hg, fasting glucose >=7 mmol/L, any medical condition that may affect results, interfering medication, HRT. Age 56.8 +/- 0.83 y and BMI 22.3 +/- 0.29 kg/m2 are printed as mean +/- SEM (Table 1); SD computed here as SEM x sqrt(34): 0.83 x 5.831 = 4.84 y and 0.29 x 5.831 = 1.69 kg/m2. Observed min/max not printed.

protocols.name: screening_fasted
protocols.description: Screening and consent visit 'following an overnight fast' (Methods, Study population and recruitment): seated resting blood pressure (Omron HEM907) and fasting glucose (HemoCue 201) measured there; Table 1 ('Subjects' baseline characteristics') does not itself say when its values were taken, and the method and time of the heart-rate reading are not described. Entered as a fasted morning with water only: clock hour (08:00), fast length (10 h, 'overnight') and a 30-minute run-in standing for the single measurement are the guide's defaults.
